decisions.reason: As a newly launched resin injection unit in the firm’s core application domain, it is likely to be retained because there is no clear evidence yet of performance below aspiration levels and the firm has enough engineering and service slack to continue learning from the market.

This product also fits the established coating and material-processing business, so absent visible signs of a shortfall against aspirations, management would usually keep it on the market while gathering more sales and customer feedback.

An automatic airless spray gun is close to the firm’s core competence and customer base, making continued support likely because established German machinery firms typically give such core products more time before considering withdrawal.

A manual airless spray gun is highly consistent with the firm’s existing product logic and installed customer needs, so behavioral-theory reasoning suggests little pressure to drop it after only a short time on the market.

Because this air-assisted airless spray gun is a whole product line with several models and strong strategic fit to the firm’s application equipment business, management is very likely to keep it unless clear underperformance emerges.

The data logger is somewhat more uncertain than the mechanical equipment because it extends into digital monitoring, but the firm still has enough complementary capability and slack to keep it while testing customer acceptance.
